The team would use data such as chronic absenteeism and test scores to identify K-5 students who are struggling academically or behaviorally, and provide support services. It runs August 31, 2020 through May 31, 2021 and is capped at $65,000. The Board is approving it after the start date.

The district pays nothing. The term is July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2023, and the text does not describe what the COVID amendment changes.

output.summary: The Board accepts a $34,852 grant from the U.S. Department of Education's Title VI Indian Education Program. The money supports academic tutoring and enrichment for Native American students. It covers July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021.

output.summary: The Board approves an amendment adding 92 calendar days to Anthonio, Inc.'s agreement to serve as inspector of record (IOR) on the Fruitvale Elementary School fire and intrusion alarm replacement. output.headline: Ratifies up to $33,000 for HERO's mentoring and leadership programs at Horace Mann Elementary
output.summary: The Board ratifies a 2020-21 contract with HERO to provide mentoring services to Title I, Latino, African American and second-language students at Horace Mann Elementary School. Services include social skills lessons, a leadership program, mentoring, staff training and organized recess. It runs August 10, 2020 through May 28, 2021 and is capped at $33,000. The Board is approving it after the start date.

output.summary: The Board approves an amendment adding 92 calendar days to Johnson Controls Fire Protection's agreement, in which it serves as inspector of record (IOR) on the Fruitvale Elementary School fire and intrusion alarm replacement. The end date moves from October 31, 2020 to January 31, 2021. The text states no added cost.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $20,000 to redesign 6th grade onboarding and orientation at Elmhurst United Middle
output.summary: The Board ratifies a 2020-21 contract to re-design how Elmhurst United Middle School engages, onboards and orients its 6th grade students. It runs October 1, 2020 through May 28, 2021 and is capped at $20,000. The Board is approving it after the start date.

output.headline: Adds $4,400 to Integral Group's Fremont High building envelope review contract
output.summary: The Board approves an amendment adding $4,400 to Integral Group's agreement for the Fremont High School new construction project, raising the limit from $313,925 to $318,325. The added work includes more building envelope commissioning (checking the building's outer shell), reviewing requests for information, drawings and architect instructions about a breezeway joint.

output.headline: Extends Jensen Hughes' Fruitvale alarm project agreement by 92 days
output.summary: The Board approves Amendment No. 7 adding 92 calendar days to Jensen Hughes' agreement for services on the Fruitvale Elementary School fire and intrusion alarm replacement. The end date moves from October 31, 2020 to January 31, 2021. The text states no added cost.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $14,000 for Oakland Youth Chorus to run a choral music program at Bret Harte Middle
output.summary: The Board ratifies a 2020-21 contract with Oakland Youth Chorus to design and run a school choral music program at Bret Harte Middle School. The group would provide music lessons that meet state arts standards, hire and train music teachers, and evaluate the program. It runs August 10, 2020 through May 31, 2021 and is capped at $14,000. The Board is approving it after the start date.

output.summary: The Board ratifies a 2020-21 contract for a contractor in the Office of Equity to attend Oakland Fund for Children and Youth (OFCY) meetings and trainings, build attendance and activity reports for OFCY high school sites, and lead weekly one-hour life skills workshops for up to 25 students. It runs September 15, 2020 through June 30, 2021 and is capped at $25,000. The Board is approving it after the start date.

output.summary: The Board approves a competitively bid contract with Data Media Services, the lowest responsive and responsible bidder, to install eleven exterior cameras and program the servers and software at Glenview Elementary School. The $50,000 includes a $5,000 contingency. Work is scheduled from October 29, 2020 to January 27, 2021.

output.headline: Moves $3,500 at Oakland High from field trip costs to extend a classroom management consultant
output.summary: The Board approves, on the Measure N Commission's recommendation, moving $3,500 from admission fees and transportation costs, unused because there are no in-person field trips, to a classroom management consultant contract. The contract term grows from one semester to the full year, August 10, 2020 through June 30, 2021.

output.headline: Moves $6,791 at Ralph Bunche Academy from culinary food costs to a case manager
output.summary: The Board approves, on the Measure N Commission's recommendation, moving $6,791 from food purchases for the culinary program, which will cost less during distance learning, to hire a case manager through Bay Area Community Resources. The case manager will help students finish pathway requirements and move on to college or careers.

output.headline: Moves $2,209 at Ralph Bunche Academy from a counselor salary to a case manager
output.summary: The Board approves, on the Measure N Commission's recommendation, moving $2,209 from a counselor's salary to hire a case manager through Bay Area Community Resources. The case manager will help students finish pathway requirements and move on to college or careers.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $4,850 for Oakland Public Education Fund to pay hotel stays for homeless families
output.summary: The Board ratifies a 2020-21 contract with Oakland Public Education Fund to process direct payments to hotels and motels for families who were moved from living in cars to temporary respite housing. The goal is to help keep distance learning stable for those students. It runs August 10, 2020 through September 30, 2020 and is capped at $4,850. The Board is approving it after the start date.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $34,475 for Cityspan software to track after-school and summer attendance
output.summary: The Board ratifies a 2020-21 contract with Cityspan Technologies for licensed software, hosting and user support. The software collects student-level attendance data and produces reports on district after-school and summer programs that meet state and federal requirements. It runs October 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021 and is capped at $34,475. The Board is approving it after the start date.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $58,153.68 for a FoodCorps member for school meals and health education
output.summary: The Board ratifies a 2020-21 contract with FoodCorps to provide a FoodCorps member who works on hands-on learning, healthy school meals and a schoolwide culture of health. It runs August 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021 and is capped at $58,153.68. The Board is approving it after the start date.

output.headline: Approves intern and practicum partnership with Reach Institute for School Leadership through June 2023
output.summary: The Board approves a memorandum of understanding (MOU) and interagency agreement with Reach Institute for School Leadership. Reach Institute would provide an intern program and a practicum (supervised training) program for people working toward teaching, counseling, school psychology, administrative and other student-support credentials. It covers July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2023. The text does not state a dollar amount.

output.headline: Approves up to $57,500 for daily student support groups and parent outreach at Franklin Elementary
output.summary: The Board approves a 2020-21 contract for daily support groups and one-on-one help for "At Promise" students at Franklin Elementary School, plus phone and home contact with parents, staff training, and parent workshops in families' home languages. It runs August 5, 2020 through May 28, 2021 and is capped at $57,500. The work began before the Board's approval.

output.headline: Amends the Board policy on giving medication to students and monitoring health conditions
output.summary: The Board adopts an amendment to Board Policy 5141.21, which covers how the district administers medication to students and monitors their health conditions. The text does not describe the specific changes.

output.headline: Approves intern and practicum partnership with University of San Francisco through June 2023
output.summary: The Board approves a memorandum of understanding (MOU) and interagency agreement with the University of San Francisco. The university would provide an intern program and a practicum (supervised training) program for people working toward teaching, counseling, school psychology, administrative and other student-support credentials. It covers July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2023. The text does not state a dollar amount.

output.headline: Approves up to $46,000 for Servio Consulting to build an after-school program planning tool
output.summary: The Board approves a 2020-21 contract with Servio Consulting, LLC to create an after-school program planning tool in Salesforce Quip. The tool would use collected data to generate after-school agreement packets and send them out for electronic signature through DocuSign. It runs October 28, 2020 through June 30, 2021 and is capped at $46,000.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $50,000 for Syntex Global translators at special education meetings
output.summary: The Board ratifies a 2020-21 contract with Syntex Global, Inc. to provide extra translators (Arabic, Spanish, Vietnamese, Chinese, Cambodian and other languages) when district need is greater than its own translators can cover, plus technical support. The translators serve legally required Individualized Education Program (IEP) meetings for students with disabilities. It runs July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021 and is capped at $50,000. The Board is approving it after the start date.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $45,000 for a distance-learning engagement mentor at West Oakland Middle
output.summary: The Board ratifies a 2020-21 contract for a person to work closely with a group of students at West Oakland Middle School. The work includes guiding students and families through distance learning, building healthy peer relationships and executive functioning skills, helping teachers in virtual classrooms, and working with African American students on leadership and Black cultural pride. It runs August 20, 2020 through May 31, 2021 and is capped at $45,000. The Board is approving it after the start date.

output.headline: Pays Santa Clara County Office of Education up to $949 for a teacher's arts lesson-plan training
output.summary: The Board ratifies a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with the Santa Clara County Office of Education. Under it, an OUSD teacher takes part in a statewide arts training module (CCSESA Arts Module 22) and produces two media arts lesson plans for its resources page. It runs September 28, 2020 through October 16, 2020 and is capped at $949. The Board is approving it after the start date.

output.headline: Amends the Board policy on gifts, grants and bequests to speed up grant acceptance
output.summary: The Board approves an update to Board Policy 3290 on gifts, grants and bequests. The change is meant to streamline how grants are accepted while keeping appropriate Board oversight.

output.headline: Amends the Board policy on contracts to streamline the contract approval process
output.summary: The Board approves an update to Board Policy 3312, which covers contracts and delegation of authority. The change is meant to streamline contract approval and to answer questions staff often ask, inside the policy itself.

output.headline: Amends the Board policy on claims against the district to streamline settlements
output.summary: The Board approves an update to Board Policy 3320 on claims and actions against the district. The change is meant to streamline the settlement process while keeping adequate Board oversight.
